name: Manaslu Circuit
summary: A remote circuit trek around Mount Manaslu (8,163m), the world's eighth-highest mountain, through the Manaslu Conservation Area near the Tibetan border. Known for fewer crowds than Everest or Annapurna, rich Tibetan-Buddhist and Gurung culture, and the high-altitude Larkya La Pass crossing.

best_time_to_visit.primary: September to November (autumn) and March to May (spring)
best_time_to_visit.notes: Autumn offers the most stable weather and clearest mountain views. Spring brings blooming rhododendron forests and milder temperatures. Winter (Dec-Feb) sees heavy snowfall that can close Larkya La Pass. Monsoon (Jun-Aug) brings heavy rain, leeches, landslides, and obscured mountain views.

route_from_kathmandu.trailhead: Machha Khola (also Soti Khola or Jagat, depending on itinerary)
transport_options: Public bus: 9-12 hours from Kathmandu's bus park (Macha Pokhari), via Dhading Besi and Arughat
Private jeep: 7-10 hours, more flexible and comfortable
route_from_kathmandu.return_point: Dharapani or Tiliche, jeep back to Kathmandu takes 8-10 hours via Besisahar

difficulty_notes: Requires good physical fitness and proper acclimatization. Highest point is Larkya La Pass (5,106m). Most trekking days involve 6-8 hours of walking on steep, rocky, sometimes exposed terrain. No technical climbing skills needed. Solo trekking is not permitted (minimum 2 trekkers plus licensed guide required by law).
time_required: 12-18 days depending on itinerary; 14 days is the most common standard length including acclimatization days
permits_required: Manaslu Restricted Area Permit (RAP) - required between Jagat and Dharapani
Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) - required for the final section near Dharapani
permit_notes: Must be arranged through a government-registered trekking agency; individual/independent application is not allowed. A licensed guide is mandatory. As of March 2026, the historical 2-trekker minimum group requirement was reportedly relaxed by Nepal's Department of Immigration, though a licensed guide remains mandatory - this rule area is still evolving and should be double-checked against current government sources before travel.
estimated_cost_usd: 700-1100+ for a 12-14 day guided package (varies by agency, inclusions, season)
culture_notes: Trail passes through Gurung and Tibetan-influenced villages, with Buddhist monasteries and mani walls, especially in the upper Nubri and Tsum areas. Community-based teahouse lodging is available along most of the route.
data_confidence_notes: Permit rule details (group-size minimum) vary across sources and appear to be changing as of 2026 - flagged as a live example of conflicting/outdated source data for eval purposes.
